hierarchy.notes: A GitHub-first identity surface that preserves CLI history and keeps identity proof separate from usage truth.

forbidden_imports: blue-check state derived from session metadata alone

classification.notes: The browser briefly receives a Supabase access token and OAuth provider token. The provider token is sent once to the trusted link endpoint and is never persisted by this module.

ssa_v2.notes: Session derivation, provider availability, global status, account interaction, and server status lookup are separated into focused files; the largest source file is 245 lines.

ssi.notes: The console reuses the existing GitHub link endpoint and Supabase browser client instead of duplicating migration logic.

sstf.notes: Focused contracts cover sanitization, redirect safety, status authorization, one-time linking, local sign-out, CLI fallback, responsive layout, and motion safety.

spe.notes: Provider settings are fetched once, auth state is subscription-driven, and link status is a bounded same-origin request.

srs.notes: Signed-out, checking, unavailable, session-only, linking, linked, migration, and error states are all visible; no auth failure is silently converted to success.

ssra.notes: Focused tests, release gate, production builds, immutable preview, account interaction, mobile/desktop/4K layout proof, and live CLI start/poll/rejection probes pass. Browser OAuth remains visibly unavailable because no dedicated GitHub OAuth app is configured; GitHub CLI sign-in is the live account-free path.

sas.notes: Account, status, and contract surfaces have explicit leases and an owned-path manifest; unrelated logo work remains outside this brick.

sva.notes: The server validates bearer sessions, returns only sanitized identity fields, and the client never persists raw provider credentials or infers a blue check from metadata.

srls.notes: The status endpoint validates the user with Supabase Auth before a service-role identity lookup; anonymous status reads fail closed.

sev.notes: Public Supabase configuration is guarded client-side, the service-role key is secret-scoped in Netlify, and live invalid-token/session probes fail without returning credentials.

ssc.notes: The slice adds no dependency and reuses the existing Next, React, Supabase, and telemetry stack.

sai.notes: Intent, owned files, current-tree gates, provider blocker, and identity/usage boundary are captured in the Gen3 receipts and this manifest.

negative_tests: unlinked session returns no identity row

code_budget.notes: The implementation is split across the route, pure session helper, global control, server status endpoint, styles, and focused contracts.

verification.command: focused auth tests + pnpm sma:release-gate + pnpm build + pnpm --dir packages/web build
verification.notes: 11 focused auth tests, 15 control-plane tests, 600 package tests, strict telemetry with zero violations, typecheck, root build, Next production build, and high-severity dependency audit pass. Netlify deploy 6a561d9d27546731cca4f52a is live; CLI start returns 200, poll remains pending without a token, invalid GitHub verification and browser sessions return 401 without credentials, and mobile/desktop/4K interaction proofs pass without horizontal overflow.

adaptation_points: Create a dedicated GitHub OAuth app for the target Supabase callback.
Configure the GitHub provider and production redirect allowlist.
Retain the immutable GitHub subject as the account migration anchor.
install_steps: Copy the account, global control, browser auth, and status surfaces.
Connect the existing identity-link endpoint and Supabase environment.
Configure a dedicated OAuth provider, then rerun live auth proof.
known_traps: Do not reuse another product's OAuth credentials or callback.
Do not store provider tokens or service-role credentials in the browser.
Do not use identity verification as proof of usage volume or leaderboard tier.

verification.notes: Current-tree release gate passed before manifest registration.
